Ф 0. J. nnd T. and A0. — Heinrich von Rosenberg und Albert von Payreschau schenken dem Abi und Convent zu Hohenfurt die Kirche in Strobnüz.

XXXIII. Cum eorum que geruntur in tempore, obliuio solet memoriam resecare, necesse est, ea tam testium quam scripture memoria con firmari. Vnde nouerint vniuersi Christi fideles presens seriptum visuri et audituri, quod nos H. de Rosenberg de consensu et voluntate vxoris mee Elyzabeth et Albertus de Borischoue de bona ac piavxo- ris mee Petronille filiique mei Hogerii voluntate venerabili domino abbati totique conuentui in Altovado pro nostra nostrorumque ante- cessorum presencium futurorumque amicorum salute animarum eccle- siam in Strobeniz omni jure, quo aprogenitoribus nostrispossedimus et a nobis ceteri possederunt, perpetuo tradidimus possidendam, vt nobis in Christo dilecti confratres nostri ibidem deo jugiter seruien- tes ex tali ac tanto elemosinarum beneficio plurimorum indigentias releuare atque ad dei seruicium pro viuurum et mortuorum salute feruentius et salubrius valeant frequentare. In cuius rei testimonium litteras presentes nostrorum munimine sigiliorum contulimus robo- ratas. Huius facti testes sunt: DominusBertholdus plebanuseiusdem ecclesie, Dominus Conradus plebanus de Ragizz, Dominus Jucobus plebanus de Rosenberg, Andreas miles de Hossicz, Rodengerus de Haichenpach, Hainricus de Altenburg. entries.english:
Heinrich von Rosenberg and Albert von Payreschau donate the church at Strobnitz to the abbot and convent of Hohenfurt.

Because forgetfulness is wont to erase the memory of what is done in time, it is necessary to confirm such matters through the memory both of witnesses and of writing. Therefore, let all the faithful of Christ who see or hear this present document know that we, H. de Rosenberg, with the consent and will of my wife Elyzabeth, and Albert de Borischoue, with the good will and consent of my wife Petronilla and my son Hoger, have forever handed over the church at Strobeniz, with every right by which our ancestors possessed it and others held it from us, to the venerable lord abbot and the whole convent at Altovado, for the salvation of the souls of ourselves, our predecessors, and our friends, present and future. Thus may our brothers, beloved in Christ, who continually serve God there, by this great gift of alms be able to relieve the needs of many and attend more fervently and effectively to God’s service for the salvation of the living and the dead. In testimony of this, we have caused this letter to be confirmed with the protection of our seals. Witnesses to this act are: Lord Berthold, parish priest of that church; Lord Conrad, parish priest of Ragitz; Lord Jacob, parish priest of Rosenberg; Andreas miles of Hossitz; Rodengerus of Haichenpach; and Hainricus of Altenburg.

Two well-preserved seals in white wax hang from yellow, green, and black silk. (a) Fairly large: a mounted rider, whose horse covering is strewn with roses, holds a sword in his right hand and a shield bearing a five-petaled rose in his left; the rider’s helmet has fan-shaped decoration. Inscription: “Seal of Heinrich, Lord of Rosenberch.” (b) Small: a shield with an arrow. Inscription: “Seal of Albert of Strobnitz.”
